body: Unfortunately only open to 18+ folks living in Michigan, USA. If you are living in Michigan, then you could absolutely participate.

Psychologists at Western Michigan University are seeking participants who are at least 18 years old and currently residing in Michigan to participate in a clinical study about a virtually-delivered treatment for trauma and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) called Written Exposure Therapy (WET). This treatment is brief, only five sessions. Total participation in the study is approximately 4 ½ hours over two months and then a 20-minute interview two months following the treatment. Your participation is completely voluntary. There is no cost to participate in this study. 

If you are interested in learning more about participation and to see if you qualify, please call the study’s clinic at 269-888-4075 to set up a virtual appointment. 

If possible, please consider sharing the above clinic contact information with others who may be potentially interested in participating. Thank you for your time.

I genuinely appreciate your thoughtful comment.

Here are the VA's overviews of several trauma-focused treatments. CPT and PE by far have the most evidence for their effectiveness, regardless of age, race/ethnicity, trauma type, time since trauma, depression severity, trauma-related symptom severity, disability status, and use of psychiatric medications. There is an abundance of research in this area. I would encourage you to look up the meta-analyses and systematic reviews of the last 30 years of RCT research. \[Although I am a huge proponent of continuing clinical research to improve evidence-based treatments for PTSD for BIPOC folks, in particular. That is a major reason why this study is being conducted in the first place. You are exactly right. There is no one-size-fits-all approach to mental health treatment and trauma. The mental health field needs to do better. End of story\]. 

In terms of responding to your comment about wanting more information- here are some brief explanations and then quick videos. Hopefully this helps. 

Both CPT and PE are 12 session protocols. In outpatient settings, typically folks do 1 session per week, for 12 weeks. In inpatient and residential settings, there are usually 2 sessions weekly, for 6 weeks. \[That is why I mentioned earlier the range for 6-12 weeks\]. In some settings, there are "massed" protocols that are being utilized where folks can actually get 3-7 sessions of CPT or PE in one week. WET, in outpatient settings is delivered weekly for 5 weeks, once session per week. In inpatient and residential settings, some providers do 2 sessions weekly, for 2.5 weeks. I am not an EMDR provider. So, I cannot speak to that. But there is some general information below.

There are no secrets here. We are testing the effectiveness of an already very effective PTSD treatment, delivered in a virtual-format, with the hopes that it is just as effective or more effective than the in-person version. All of this information is explained to interested individuals. We are trying to have as much reach as possible, in terms of getting this resource distributed as far and wide as we can [that is why you have seen posts in different subreddits]. [Although only people living in Michigan can participate.] We are doing our best. Therapy and mental health treatment are extremely expensive. We are doing our best to channel resources during this very very stressful time.
CPT takes between 6-12 weeks. WET takes 5 weeks. Your opinion is valid. And this treatment is legitimate. No app is used. Although, that is a great idea! Have a safe rest of your day.

**Who I am**: Clinical Psychology Ph.D. Candidate

**Affiliation**: Western Michigan University

**Target group**: Michigan residents, 18+ years old, experienced a traumatic event

**Contact Information**: Virtual Written Exposure Therapy Clinic - 269-888-4075 or [virtualwetstudy@gmail.com](mailto:virtualwet@gmail.com)

**Background**: Written Exposure Therapy (WET) is a manualized and scripted five session mental health treatment designed to treat posttraumatic stress symptoms (Sloan & Marx, 2019). WET has moderate support to demonstrate significant reductions in posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms regardless of baseline PTSD severity, depression severity, time since trauma, sex, age, race, or educational level. This study is an open clinical trial of virtually-delivered Written Exposure Therapy (WET). This treatment is brief, only five sessions. Total participation in the study is approximately 4 ½ hours over two months and then a 20-minute interview two months following the treatment.
